summary: CCC-built three-story 1941-43 lookout near Yellowstone, with a 1962 visitor center added and volunteer staffing since 1975.

facts.design: three-story wood-sided structure of 8x8 beams, flattop 14x14 ft cab with catwalk, 26.25 ft tall

staffing.status: staffed by volunteers during summer since 1975

access.note: visitor center and lookout open to drive-up visitors in summer, off the Beartooth Scenic Highway via a short forest road; not a rental

visit.trail_note: reached via FS Rd 142, about half a mile off US-212

events.note: construction started under the CCC program
construction completed after the CCC program was closed down (NHLR gives 1942 as the completion year)
visitor center structure added at the base
staffed by volunteers starting in 1975, continuing as of this writing

evidence.supports: used as fire detection point since early 1900s, flattop 14x14 cab with catwalk completed by CCC 1942, visitor center added 1962, staffed by volunteers since 1975
evidence.quote: Located above the Beartooth Scenic Highway on the Shoshone National Forest in the high peaks northeast of Yellowstone National Park, Clay Butte Lookout was first used as a fire detection point in the early 1900s. The flattop 14' x 14' cab with catwalk was completed by the CCC in 1942. The visitor center structure was added at the base in 1962. A popular attraction, the site has been staffed by volunteers since 1975.

evidence.supports: construction started 1941 under CCC, unfinished when CCC closed, completed 1943, three-story wood-sided structure of 8x8 beams, 26.25 ft tall, NRHP listed Jan 8 2014, location ~16 miles east of Yellowstone, off US-212 via FS Rd 142
evidence.quote: Its construction was started in 1941 within the Civilian Conservation Corps program, but the CCC was closed before it was completed in 1943. It is a three-story wood-sided structure built out of eight inch by eight inch beams. It is 26.25 feet (8.00 m) tall.

evidence.supports: staffed with volunteers during summer, named personnel 1980 Fred & Jeannette Fell, located 40 miles NW of Cody, Park County Wyoming
evidence.quote: This 3-story concrete tower w/ live-in cab is staffed with volunteers during the summer. Known lookout personnel: 1980: Fred & Jeannette Fell.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives a single completion year of 1942; Wikipedia (citing the NRHP nomination) says construction started in 1941 under the CCC and was finished in 1943 after the CCC program ended. Both describe the same build; this story follows the more detailed NRHP-sourced account.

firelookout.com describes the tower as concrete; the NRHP nomination (via Wikipedia) describes a wood-sided structure built from 8x8-inch beams. The story follows the NRHP description as the more authoritative, documented source.

notes_for_editor: Height_m taken from Wikipedia's 26.25 ft (8.00 m) structure height, not from ground elevation. Material conflict (wood vs concrete) flagged but not independently resolved beyond preferring the NRHP-sourced Wikipedia account.
